passages.title: David’s Rise to Power over Israel.
passages.text: The Chronicler focuses on Israel’s unity under David, passing over most of the conflict with Saul and Ishbosheth that 2 Samuel describes.

passages.title: 1 Chron 10:1–12
passages.text: Taken mainly from 1 Sam. 31:1–13 . Saul’s reign ends in disaster for Israel at the hands of the **Philistines** ( 1 Chron. 10:7 ). His death, along with the deaths of three of his sons, marks the end of his royal house (v. 6 ). **temple of Dagon** (v. 10 ). Saul’s humiliation after his death contrasts with the triumph of the ark over Dagon in 1 Sam. 5:1–4 .

passages.title: 1 Chron 10:11–12
passages.text: Saul had saved **Jabesh-gilead** earlier ( 1 Samuel 11 ). This explains why the city gave a proper burial to Saul and his sons. David later reburied their bones ( 2 Sam. 21:14 ).

passages.title: 1 Chron 10:13–14
passages.text: **his breach of faith** (compare 2:7 ; 5:25 ; 9:1 ). Saul failed to **keep the command of the Lord** (see 1 Sam. 13:13 ). He consulted the **medium** of En-dor ( 1 Samuel 28 ) but did not **seek** the Lord. His sin caused his death. **turned the kingdom over to David**. This is the main point of the chapter.

notes.text: **Saul took his own sword and fell upon it**. See note on 2 Sam. 1:6–10 for the claim that Saul did not commit suicide but rather was killed by an Amalekite.
